anomalies.observed: On the Water Level sheet, the TF-Luna LiDAR symbol PR1 is drawn wired to header H1 (PB_1.25mm): its VCC/SDA/SCL/GND pins carry +5V, I2C_SDA, I2C_SCL and GND, and its TX pin is tied to the EZO_PDIS net (the same net that drives IO6/SPI_CLK and the PDIS pins 8 of U3/U4).
anomalies.expected: The specification states PR1 is excluded from the board and electrically absent: 'PR1 with on_board: no ... all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.' EZO_PDIS should only connect IO6/SPI_CLK to U3.8 and U4.8, and the main I2C bus should not be loaded by a 5V LiDAR.

evidence.quote: Water Level Sensor/Switches sheet: 'PR1 LiDAR' symbol with pins VCC/SDA/SCL/GND/TX wired to 'H1 PB_1.25mm', whose nets are labelled '+5V', 'I2C_SDA', 'I2C_SCL' and 'EZO_PDIS'.
§4.3 / §6: 'the r2 netlist shows PR1 with on_board: no ... and all four pins (VCC, SDA, SCL, GND) typed free — i.e., it is not connected to any net in this design.'

anomalies.impact: A component intended to be absent is now electrically present: a 5V TF-Luna is hung on the 3.3V-pulled I2C bus, and the ESP32-driven EZO_PDIS line (which also powers-disables the pH/EC isolators) is shorted to the LiDAR's TX output, producing contention on the isolator-enable net and possible I2C level/communication faults.

parsed.summary: The build deviates from the intended design by wiring the TF-Luna LiDAR (PR1/H1) into the main I2C bus and, most tellingly, into the EZO_PDIS control net, whereas the specification documents PR1 as excluded from the board with all pins free and EZO_PDIS driving only U3/U4 PDIS; this creates bus contention and a 5V-on-3.3V I2C mismatch.
